problem: The turn-off does not show ZCS. The gate pulse bar ends at 7.5 µs while the switch-current lane still shows 5 A up to 7.5 µs, and the current only reaches 0 A at 8 µs, when the voltage rises. Section 2 states the opposite rule: a resonant pulse brings the switch current to zero before the gate is removed. As drawn, the gate is removed while 5 A flows and the current then falls with the voltage still at 0 V, which is a capacitive (ZVS-type) turn-off, not a ZCS turn-off.
fix: Bring the switch current to 0 A at 7.5 µs and keep the gate on until 7.5–8 µs, so the current reaches zero first and the gate is removed afterwards; the voltage then rises at 8 µs. Also close the two unlabelled gaps in the current lane (2.5–3 µs and 7.5–8 µs).

where: Section 1, note after the P_sw formula
problem: "The ½ assumes a triangular voltage-current overlap" can be read as voltage and current ramping together over the same interval. If both ramped together the energy would be V·I·t/6, not ½·V·I·t. The ½ in the standard formula comes from one quantity ramping while the other stays fixed.
fix: Say: at turn-on the current ramps to I while the freewheeling diode clamps the voltage at V; at turn-off the voltage ramps to V while the current stays at I. The instantaneous power pulse is triangular in each case, giving ½·V·I·t_r and ½·V·I·t_f.

problem: "Moving f_s away from f_0 lowers the gain" is true only above resonance. Below f_0 an LLC gain curve rises above 1 to a peak before dropping, and that boost region is exactly how the converter holds output when the input sags. The sentence as written hides this.
fix: Say: raising f_s above f_0 lowers the gain; lowering f_s below f_0 raises the gain up to a peak set by Q, then the gain falls again. Operation below f_0 is how the LLC boosts, and its usable window is bounded by that peak.
